releases.notes:
# Borderless Window 1.9.0 *NeoForge · Fabric 1.21.1 · 2026-11-08* > **Now on Fabric too.** The same mod, with every feature, for both loaders. Without Sodium, it now also lives in Minecraft's own Video Settings, and it has a logo of its own. ## ⚠️ Important Notes - **The jar has a new name**: `borderlesswindow-neoforge-1.9.0+mc1.21.1.jar` (or `-fabric-`). When updating, delete the old `borderlesswindow-1.8.0.jar` from your mods folder so the mod is not loaded twice - Settings carry over untouched: both loaders read the same `config/borderlesswindow.json`, so you can even move a setup from one to the other - **On Fabric there is nothing else to install.** Fabric API is not required: the one piece the mod needs from it, to load its translations, is bundled inside the jar, as Sodium does. If you already have Fabric API, they get along - Nothing changes in how the mod behaves on NeoForge ## ✨ New Features ### Fabric support - Every feature works on **Fabric 1.21.1** (Fabric Loader 0.16.0 or newer): screen modes and F11, the FPS counter and the background options, fog, clouds, screen and camera overlays, field of view, distortion, bobbing, distances and enchantment numerals - The **Sodium** integration is the same: the Screen Mode selector in its video settings and the mod's six pages - With **Mod Menu** installed, the mod's entry in its list opens the config screen, like NeoForge's Config button. Mod Menu is optional ### Minecraft's Video Settings - Without Sodium, the **Fullscreen** toggle in Minecraft's Video Settings becomes a **Screen Mode** selector: Windowed, Borderless or Fullscreen. It applies at once and follows F11 while the screen is open - **Fullscreen Resolution** is greyed out unless the mode is Fullscreen, the only mode it applies to, as on the mod's Sodium page - A **Borderless Window...** button at the end of the list opens the full config screen - So the mod can be set up entirely from Minecraft's own menus on both loaders, with no other mod. With Sodium installed nothing changes here: its video settings replace this screen, and the mod's options are in its pages as before ### Logo - The mod has a logo now, a grass block with arrows pointing out to the corners, shown in NeoForge's mod list and in Mod Menu ## 🔧 Technical Changes - The project is now multiloader, after jaredlll08's MultiLoader-Template: `common/` holds nearly all the code and is compiled against plain Minecraft, so a loader-specific call there fails to build; `neoforge/` and `fabric/` only add each loader's entry point and hooks - On Fabric, fog, the water and fire overlays, the FPS counter and startup are hooked with the mod's own mixins rather than Fabric API events. The saved screen mode is applied on the second frame, once the window is up, so it opens straight in Borderless - The config file path now comes from the game directory rather than a NeoForge API; it is the same folder as before - One branch per Minecraft version (`NeoFabric/1.21.1`), with release tags such as `v1.9.0+mc1.21.1`. Every build makes both jars, and `[curseforge]` uploads each one with its loader - Gradle 9.8, Fabric Loom 1.16, and stable Parchment mappings for 1.21.1 ## 📦 Dependencies - Minecraft 1.21.1 with NeoForge 21.1.x, or with Fabric Loader 0.16.0 or newer - Optional: Sodium 0.8.x on either loader, and Mod Menu on Fabric ---

Sin Sodium, ahora también vive en los Ajustes de video del propio Minecraft, y tiene un logo propio. ## ⚠️ Notas Importantes - **El jar tiene un nombre nuevo**: `borderlesswindow-neoforge-1.9.0+mc1.21.1.jar` (o `-fabric-`). Al actualizar, borra el viejo `borderlesswindow-1.8.0.jar` de tu carpeta de mods para que el mod no se cargue dos veces ...

releases.notes:
# Borderless Window 1.8.0 *NeoForge 1.21.1 · 2026-11-08* > **The game rests when you are not looking.** Three new background options join the Unfocused FPS Limit on their own page, Minecraft's glint and menu blur sliders come back to Sodium's video settings, and every slider now moves in steps of 1. ## ⚠️ Important Notes - Every option keeps its ID, so existing settings carry over untouched. Every new option defaults to Minecraft's behavior - **Dynamic FPS** no longer greys out the background options. Both mods can now be used together: frame rate caps stack and the lower one wins. If both lower the background volume, the reductions multiply, so it is best to set the volume in only one of them ## ✨ New Features ### Background - **Unfocused Volume**: lowers the game volume while its window is not focused — after Alt+Tab, while minimized, or with another window or monitor in front. It is a share of your Master Volume, from 0 (Muted) to 100%, the default. Full volume returns as soon as you click back in, and sounds that start while muted (music, ambient loops) are there when you return - **Pause Rendering When Minimized**: stops drawing frames while the window is minimized and slows the game loop to 10 FPS. The game itself keeps running — the world, sounds and multiplayer connections are unaffected; only the picture stops until you restore the window. Off by default - **Idle FPS Limit**: after a number of minutes with no keyboard or mouse input (1 to 30, Off by default), the frame rate is capped at a value you choose (5 to 60 FPS, 30 by default) — even while the window is focused. Any key, click, scroll or mouse movement lifts it at once. Gamepad input from controller mods does not count as activity - When several limits apply at once, the lowest wins ### Enchantments and menus - New **Enchantments** page holding the Enchantment Numerals option, plus Minecraft's own **Glint Speed** and **Glint Strength** sliders, which Sodium's video settings leave out. Glint Strength applies instantly, no restart needed - Minecraft's **Menu Background Blur** slider is back too, on the General page - Like the FOV and Distortion Effects sliders, these are the same settings found under Accessibility and are saved with Minecraft's options, not the mod's ### Sliders and pages - Every slider now moves in steps of 1: percentages by 1%, distances by 1 block, FPS limits by 1 FPS. The Unfocused FPS Limit still starts at 5 FPS: below 2 FPS Minecraft falls behind on client ticks, and 5 keeps a comfortable margin - The mod's Sodium section now has six pages: **General** (F11, menu blur), **Enchantments**, **FPS & Background**, **Visual Effects**, **Camera** and **Distances**. The no-Sodium config screen follows the same order, with a new **Background** header ## 🔧 Technical Changes - New `sound/` package with `UnfocusedVolumeState`; `fps/` gains `MinimizedRenderState` and `IdleFpsState` - New mixins: `ListenerMixin` (scales only the OpenAL gain, never the listener's stored value, so sounds still start while muted), `SoundManagerAccessor`, `MouseHandlerMixin` and `KeyboardHandlerMixin` (input activity). `MinecraftMixin` now also wraps `GameRenderer.render` in `runTick` and handles focus changes - The README and the changelogs are now split by language: `README_ES.md`, and an index in `CHANGELOG.md` / `CHANGELOG_ES.md` ## 📦 Dependencies - No changes: NeoForge 21.1.x, and optionally Sodium 0.8.x ---
🇪🇸 Leer en español > **El juego descansa cuando no lo estás viendo.** Tres opciones nuevas de segundo plano se suman al Límite de FPS sin foco en su propia página, los sliders de brillo y de desenfoque de menús de Minecraft vuelven a los ajustes de video de Sodium, y todos los sliders ahora van de 1 en 1. ## ⚠️ Notas Importantes - Todas las opciones conservan su ID, así que los ajustes que ya tenías se mantienen. Todas las opciones nuevas vienen por defecto en el comportamiento de Minecraft ...

Every setting defaults to vanilla behavior. Optional Sodium video settings integration. Configurable from the Mods menu, no dependencies required.

releases.notes:
# 1.7.0

## Unfocused FPS limit

- New **Unfocused FPS Limit**: caps the frame rate while the game window is not focused — after Alt+Tab, while minimized, or with another window or monitor in front. Off by default, then 5 to 60 FPS in steps of 5
- Minecraft 1.21.1 keeps rendering at full speed in the background, burning GPU power and heat on frames nobody sees. 1.21.2 later added its own limit; this brings the same idea to 1.21.1
- It can only lower the frame rate: a regular Max Framerate that is already lower still wins, and menus with no world loaded keep Minecraft's own 60 FPS. The cap lifts on the very next frame after you click back into the game
- With **Dynamic FPS** installed the option steps aside and is greyed out, with a tooltip saying why. Both mods hook the same methods, and two settings fighting over one behavior would only be confusing — Dynamic FPS covers this and more

## Draw distances

- Four new sliders that stop drawing things past a distance you choose: **Dropped Items**, **Experience Orbs**, **Armor Stands** and **Particles**. Every slider starts at **Default** on the left, which keeps Minecraft's own distance
- Minecraft draws items up to 16 blocks away and orbs up to 32 (both scaled by its Entity Distance option), armor stands as far as the server sends them, and spawns particles up to 32 blocks away. These sliders can only lower those numbers
- It is purely visual: items and orbs are only hidden, never removed. Items can still be picked up, orbs still fly to you, and nothing changes for the server or other players
- **Glowing** entities are always drawn, since the outline is information meant to be seen from afar
- **Armor stands with a visible name** are always drawn: servers and adventure maps use them as floating text and holograms
- Particles are refused when they would spawn, which is where their cost is, rather than hidden while they already exist. Particles the game marks as always visible are left alone, exactly as Minecraft does with its own 32-block limit

## Sodium integration

- The mod's section went from nine pages to four: **General** (F11, FPS overlay and unfocused limit, enchantment numerals), **Visual Effects** (fog, clouds, screen overlays), **Camera** (bobbing, FOV, distortion) and **Distances**. Inside each page the features are split into groups, the same way Sodium's own General page does it
- Every option keeps its ID, so existing settings carry over untouched
- The no-Sodium config screen follows the same order, keeping its per-feature headers

## Internal

- New `distance/` package; `fps/` gains `UnfocusedFpsState`
- New mixins: `MinecraftMixin` (`getFramerateLimit`), `EntityRenderDispatcherMixin` (`shouldRender`) and `LevelRendererMixin` (`addParticleInternal`). Sodium's entity culling wraps the frustum test one call deeper, inside `EntityRenderer.shouldRender`, so the two stack cleanly
- New generic `IntOptionSlider` for the no-Sodium screen: a stepped integer slider with the label supplied by the caller. Arrow keys move one whole step instead of vanilla's one pixel
- New `build.yml` workflow: builds every push and pull request to `master` and keeps the jar as an artifact for 14 days. A commit message containing `[curseforge]` also uploads that build to CurseForge
- Dependabot now keeps the workflow actions up to date

releases.notes:
# 1.6.1

- Fixed Portal Distortion not applying after crossing a Nether portal. You arrive standing inside the destination portal, but Minecraft ignores that portal until its cooldown runs out, so with a Nausea effect active the distortion switched to the Nausea percentage while you were still in the portal. Stepping out and back in was the only way to get the portal percentage back. Touching a portal now always counts as the portal, cooldown or not
- Corrected the 1.6.0 notes about the green nausea texture. It is not left to vanilla: Nausea Distortion drives it the same way Minecraft's own Distortion Effects slider does, so lowering Nausea Distortion trades the spinning for the green cue, and at 0% there is no spinning and the texture is at full strength. While a portal is the source, the texture follows Minecraft's slider only. The code always behaved this way; only the notes were wrong

## Internal

- New `EntityMixin` records contact with a Nether portal at the head of `setAsInsidePortal`, before vanilla's cooldown check, and `LocalPlayerMixin` counts that contact as the portal when attributing the distortion source

releases.notes:
# 1.6.0

## Camera overlays

- Added four toggles for the full-screen overlays Minecraft draws over your view: **Pumpkin**, **Freeze**, **Portal** and **Spyglass**
- **Pumpkin Overlay** removes the blur drawn while wearing a carved pumpkin, so it can be worn against endermen without the visual cost. Helmet overlays added by other mods are never affected
- **Freeze Overlay** removes the frost border drawn while freezing in powder snow. That border also warns you are taking freeze damage; the frozen hearts on the HUD still show it
- **Portal Overlay** removes the purple warp drawn while standing inside a Nether portal, which mostly gets in the way while building or aligning them
- **Spyglass Overlay** removes the scope texture and the black bars. The zoom itself is unchanged — only the frame around it is removed
- All four live in the existing Screen Overlays section, alongside the water and fire toggles
- The vignette is deliberately not offered: it doubles as the world border warning, and a plain toggle would delete that warning along with the darkening

## Field of view

- Minecraft has one **FOV Effects** slider for every source at once. It is now split into four: **Speed**, **Flying**, **Bow** and **Fluid**, each 0-100% with 100% being vanilla
- **Speed FOV** is the one worth having: with Speed potions or a modified movement attribute the FOV never settles, and until now there was no way to soften that without removing the bow zoom too
- **Flying FOV** covers creative flight only. Elytra gliding is a different thing and is not affected
- **Bow FOV** keeps the same easing curve and only changes how deep the zoom goes. The spyglass is never touched: its zoom is what the item does, not a visual effect
- **Fluid FOV** is the squeeze applied underwater and in lava
- All four sit under Minecraft's own FOV Effects slider rather than replacing it — with that at Off, nothing here has any effect

## Distortion

- Minecraft has one **Distortion Effects** slider covering both the Nether portal and the Nausea effect. It is now split into **Portal Distortion** and **Nausea Distortion**, each 0-100%
- The two share one accumulator internally, so the source is attributed per tick from the rate vanilla itself picks. Walking into a portal while under a Nausea potion correctly applies the portal percentage, and applies the Nausea one again the moment you step out
- Both sit under Minecraft's own Distortion Effects slider, same as the FOV options
- The green nausea texture is left entirely to vanilla. It is Minecraft's accessibility trade — a static cue that replaces the spinning as you lower *its* slider — and driving it from ours turned "less motion" into a bright green full-screen overlay, which is the opposite of what the option is for

## Sodium integration

- Two vanilla sliders Sodium's video settings leave out are now available inside the mod's pages: **Distortion Effects (Minecraft)** and **FOV Effects (Minecraft)**, each at the top of the page it governs so the hierarchy reads top-down
- Both are the same settings found in Minecraft's Accessibility Settings and are saved with Minecraft's options, not the mod's
- The Sodium section now has nine per-feature pages: General, FPS Overlay, Fog, Clouds, Screen Overlays, Bobbing, FOV, Distortion and Enchantment Style
- Every option remains fully available without Sodium via the Mods menu Config screen, except the two vanilla sliders above — without Sodium those are one click away in Minecraft's own menus and duplicating them would serve nobody

## Internal

- New `fov/` and `distortion/` packages; `screeneffect/` gains `CameraOverlayFilter`
- New mixins: `GuiMixin`, `AbstractClientPlayerMixin`, `LocalPlayerMixin`
- The camera overlays need bytecode rather than an event: NeoForge exposes the whole group as a single `CAMERA_OVERLAYS` GUI layer, so cancelling it would remove all of them at once. The pumpkin and freeze overlays share one vanilla method and are told apart by texture

releases.notes:
# 1.5.0 — Enchantment level numerals

Enchantment levels above X showed raw text instead of a number: a
Looting 11 book read "Looting enchantment.level.11". Levels are legal
all the way to 255, but Minecraft only ships names for the first ten.

This fixes it and adds a style option with three values:

- Mixed (default): Roman numerals up to X, plain numbers past it. This
  is the fix on its own — nothing you already see changes.
- Always Roman: generated numerals at every level, XI through CCLV.
- Always Numbers: plain numbers at every level, including 1-10.

Mixed defers to the language file whenever a translation exists, so
resource packs that do name high levels keep working. The other two are
explicit choices and always generate.

Implementation: WrapOperation (MixinExtras) wraps the single
Component.translatable call inside Enchantment.getFullname, capturing
the target method's own level parameter instead of parsing it back out
of the key. The guard above that call is untouched, so single-level
enchantments like Mending still show no number, and returning the
original Operation leaves vanilla's component identical whenever no
override applies. One injection covers item tooltips, enchanted books
and the enchanting table.

New enchantment/ package (EnchantmentLevelStyle, EnchantmentLevelState,
EnchantmentLevelFormatter) plus mixin/EnchantmentMixin, wired into both
UIs, the config file and the three lang files.
